requirements.name: Faster word-to-Chi lookup still implements semantic answer retrieval
requirements.classification: Historical reduced semantic authority; optimization is a separate property
requirements.historical_requirement_or_mechanism: The June commands replace whole-atlas scans with a lowercased word→set(Chi) index and ±2 Chi-neighborhood lookups. Section/motif records supply words; subject/verb/object recall feeds emission candidates. The earlier word→emission-section cache similarly accelerates supplied grammar routing. Exact lookup equivalence can be a legitimate computational improvement while the underlying word-address answer authority conflicts with current experience-driven native cognition.
requirements.current_disposition: These are historical code excerpts and reports, not complete current implementations or serving evidence. A reverse index is not automatically ML, and an integer neighborhood lookup is not automatically invalid for every external application. Here the described pupil decision evaluates semantic keys and a reduced Chi neighborhood instead of the full DSF relationships, retained physical contacts and actual contextual experience.
requirements.lawful_remedy: Retire legacy semantic answer authority from all current pupil paths. Preserve bounded observer/indexing techniques only where they do not choose meaning or action. Native recall must arise from retained physical state reassembled by real cues, with producer/consumer and checkpoint provenance; do not rebuild Chi tables to regain convenient words.
